# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## Primary Categories by Core Mechanic

---

### 1. LOOP-DRAWING GAMES
*The primary goal is to draw a single continuous closed loop*

#### 1.1 Unconstrained Path Loop
- **Slitherlink** – Connect dots with lines; numbers indicate how many sides of a cell the loop uses
- **Masyu** – Loop must satisfy black circle (turn + straight) and white circle (straight + turn neighbor) rules

#### 1.2 Cell-Traversal Loop
*Loop passes through cell centers*

##### 1.2.1 With Regional Constraints
- **Moon-or-Sun** – Loop passes through rooms once; must alternate between moon-only and sun-only rooms
- **Dotchi-Loop** – Loop must go straight OR turn through all white circles in each bold-line region; avoids black circles
- **Suraromu** – Loop starts/ends at numbered circle; must pass through all "Gates" in a specific order

##### 1.2.2 With Directional/Wind Constraints
- **Nagareru** – Loop direction determined by arrows; wind from black cells restricts movement direction
- **Yajilin** – Loop avoids black cells and numbered cells; arrow-numbers indicate black cell counts in a direction

##### 1.2.3 With Circle/Midpoint Constraints
- **Mid-loop** – Black circles must be the midpoint of a straight segment of the loop

---

### 2. PATH & CONNECTION GAMES
*The goal is to connect elements or move pieces along paths*

#### 2.1 Island Connection
- **Hashiwokakero** – Connect numbered islands with bridges; bridge count must match island number; all islands connected

#### 2.2 Pair Connection
- **Numberlink** – Connect matching number pairs with non-crossing, non-branching lines filling the grid

#### 2.3 Piece Movement
- **Satogaeri** – Move circles into their home regions; circles travel in straight lines and cannot cross paths
- **Yosenabe** – Move numbered circles in straight lines into gray areas; gray area numbers must match circle total sum

---

### 3. REGION DIVISION GAMES
*The goal is to partition the grid into regions satisfying given constraints*

#### 3.1 Rectangular Regions
- **Shikaku** – Divide grid into rectangles; each rectangle contains exactly one number equal to its cell count

#### 3.2 Fixed-Size Polyomino Regions
- **Five Cells** – Divide grid into pentominoes (exactly 5 cells each); numbers indicate boundary line count around a cell
- **LITS** – Color one tetromino per bold region; same-shaped tetrominoes cannot touch; colored cells form connected network with no 2×2

#### 3.3 Variable-Size Regions with Number Constraints
- **Fillomino** – Fill grid with numbered blocks; each block's size equals its number; same-sized blocks cannot touch
- **Sashigane** – Divide grid into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends; arrows point toward bends; numbers indicate block size

#### 3.4 Symmetrical/Paired Regions
- **Double Choco** – Divide grid into blocks each containing equal white and gray areas of identical shape; numbers indicate cell count per color
- **Nuritwin** – Each bold region contains exactly two same-sized shaded blocks; all shaded cells globally connected; no 2×2 shading

---

### 4. CELL-SHADING / COLORING GAMES
*The goal is to shade or paint cells according to constraints*

#### 4.1 Connectivity & Grouping Rules
- **Nurikabe** – Shade cells to form a connected "wall"; numbered white islands of exact size; no 2×2 shading
- **Heyawake** – Shade cells by room count; shaded cells cannot touch; white cells cannot span more than two rooms in a line
- **Kurotto** – Shade cells; numbered circles indicate total adjacent connected black cells; circles cannot be shaded
- **Usowan** – Shade cells; each bold region has exactly one "wrong" number among the neighbor-count clues; shaded cells cannot touch

#### 4.2 Shape-Constrained Shading
- **Choco Banana** – Shaded regions must be rectangular; white regions must be non-rectangular; numbers indicate region size
- **Norinori** – Shade cells in dominoes (pairs); each bold region must contain exactly two shaded cells

#### 4.3 Projection / Gravity Rules
- **Sto-stone** – Shade cells in rooms by count; when "dropped" downward, shaded cells must fill exactly the bottom half of the grid

#### 4.4 Tile-Based Shading
- **Tilepaint** – Entire bold-outlined tiles must be fully shaded or unshaded; diagonal-number clues indicate black cell counts in rows/columns

#### 4.5 Hitori-Style Deduplication
- **Hitori** – Shade cells so no number repeats in any row or column; shaded cells cannot touch; white cells remain connected

---

### 5. NUMBER-PLACEMENT GAMES
*The goal is to place or deduce numbers in cells*

#### 5.1 Latin Square / Uniqueness-Based
- **Sudoku** – Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 box with no repeats

#### 5.2 Region-Completion
- **Ripple Effect** – Fill rooms with consecutive numbers from 1; duplicate numbers in a row/column must be separated by at least that number of cells
- **Makaro** – Fill rooms with 1 to (room size); arrow-black-cells indicate which neighbor holds the largest value; same numbers in different rooms cannot touch

#### 5.3 Crossword-Style Numeric Fill
- **Nansuke** – Fill grid with numbers from a given list; numbers read horizontally or vertically; one digit per cell

#### 5.4 Snake/Sequential Placement
- **Hebi** – Place snake bodies (1–5) in connected sequences; snakes cannot touch each other; black-cell clues give nearest snake value in arrow direction

---

### 6. LIGHT / VISIBILITY GAMES
*The goal involves illumination or line-of-sight mechanics*

- **Akari** – Place light bulbs in white cells; numbered cells indicate adjacent bulb count; every white cell must be illuminated; bulbs cannot illuminate each other
- **Kurodoko** – Shade cells black; numbered white cells count all visible white cells horizontally and vertically; black cells cannot touch; white cells stay connected

---

### 7. SYMBOL / MARK PLACEMENT GAMES
*The goal is to place non-numeric symbols according to constraints*

#### 7.1 Directional Marks
- **Juosan** – Fill cells with — or |; regional number clues indicate the difference between the two types; marks constrained in how far they can extend perpendicularly

#### 7.2 Triangle/Geometric Marks
- **Shakashaka** – Place triangles in cells so remaining white space forms only rectangles/squares; numbers indicate adjacent triangle count

---

### 8. BLOCK / CHAIN LOGIC GAMES
*The goal involves identifying or constructing connected black-cell structures*

- **Chained Block** – Identify black-cell blocks; numbered cells indicate block size; all blocks must form diagonal-contact chains; no two blocks of the same size/shape in one chain

---

### 9. MAZE / ROUTING GAMES
*The goal involves finding or constructing a navigable path*

- **Nurimeizu** – Paint rooms to create walls; white cells form a maze from S to G; circle cells lie on shortest path; triangle cells do not; no 2×2 painted or white squares

---

### 10. PROMONTORY / ENDPOINT GAMES
*The goal involves identifying special endpoint or tip cells*

- **Nurimisaki** – Shade cells; circled cells are "Misaki" (promontories) with exactly one white neighbor; numbers indicate white cell line length from promontory; white cells stay connected; no 2×2 groups

---

### 11. DRAWING / MARKING SEQUENCE GAMES
*The goal involves placing or growing shapes in a specific sequence*

- **Evolomino** – Place squares in white cells forming blocks; each block contains one arrow; arrows must pass through ≥2 blocks; each successive block adds one square to the prior shape without rotation or flipping
- **Pencils** – Identify pencil shapes (straight groups with a tip); draw lines from tips; numbers in pencils indicate pencil length; lines cannot cross

---

## Cross-Reference: Secondary Constraint Themes

| Constraint Theme | Games Exhibiting It |
|---|---|
| No 2×2 shaded/colored blocks | Nurikabe, LITS, Nurimisaki, Nuritwin, Nurimeizu |
| Connectivity of shaded cells required | Nurikabe, LITS, Nuritwin, Kurotto |
| Connectivity of white cells required | Nurikabe, Heyawake, Hitori, Kurodoko, Nurimisaki |
| Numbers indicate neighbor counts | Akari, Shakashaka, Usowan, Five Cells |
| Single connected loop | Slitherlink, Masyu, Dotchi-Loop, Moon-or-Sun, Mid-loop, Nagareru, Yajilin, Suraromu |
| Regions/rooms with internal rules | Heyawake, Ripple Effect, Makaro, Moon-or-Sun, Nurimeizu, Sto-stone, Nuritwin |
| Directional arrow clues | Hebi, Yajilin, Makaro, Sashigane, Evolomino, Yosenabe, Nagareru |
| Movement / path tracing of pieces | Satogaeri, Yosenabe |
| Shape matching / symmetry | Double Choco, Chained Block, Evolomino, LITS |
| Gravity / projection mechanic | Sto-stone |
